transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I can’t seem to slow down with starting things. I keep launching new projects—work plans, certification schedules, upgrades to my home network, even reaching out to old contacts—and it just keeps building.

At first it feels productive, but then I blow past normal limits. My wife or my director usually has to step in and tell me to stop or pull back. It’s been getting hard to control.
Have you noticed a decreased need for sleep lately, like feeling rested after only a few hours of sleep or not feeling tired even when you don't get much sleep?
Yes. There are stretches where I’ll sleep maybe three hours, then wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning feeling sharp, like I got extra time in the day. I don’t feel tired the way I normally would.
Have you found yourself becoming unusually restless or been told that you’re moving or acting more quickly than usual?

Yes. I get really restless. I’ll pace around the house with my laptop instead of just sitting down, or I’ll start reorganizing the garage for no real reason. I’ll rewrite project boards over and over. If I try to just sit and watch a show, I feel physically uncomfortable, like I need to be doing something.
Have you noticed that your mood has been unusually high, expansive, or overly confident during these periods?

Yes. Some weeks I feel almost electric, like I can handle anything and I’m moving faster than everyone else. It feels good at first, like I’m unstoppable.

But it can flip pretty quickly. If there’s a small delay, or my wife asks me a simple question, I can snap at her because it feels like people are trying to slow me down on purpose.
Have you had any distinct periods where your mood was unusually high, excited, or irritable that lasted at least a week, even if it eventually shifted back to normal or low?

Yes, definitely. It’s not just a few hours—it can last for a week or sometimes longer. I’ll feel really charged up, almost electric, like I’m unstoppable. But I also get irritable fast. Something small, like a delay or my wife asking me a question, can make me snap because it feels like people are trying to slow me down on purpose.
After one of these high-energy, irritable periods, have you ever experienced a time where you felt very low, sad, or hopeless for at least two weeks?

Yes. After those periods, I can crash pretty hard. There are stretches where I wake up already feeling like I’ve failed at everything, like I’m just a failed version of myself. I feel heavy and flat, and even normal things—like answering my wife’s questions—can feel like too much.
Have there been times when your high energy or mood changes were so extreme that they caused serious problems at work, at home, or maybe even led to hospitalization?

Yes. It’s caused real problems. I was put on leave after a migration at work failed, and I know my judgment and pace had a lot to do with how things went.

At home, my wife has had to step in more than I’d like to admit—especially around spending, me working late into the night, and conversations that turn into arguments. And I’ve pulled back from things I used to be steady with, like church music, climbing, and mentoring, because I can’t always show up or follow through.
